title: Recurrent Neural Networks
subtitle: Contact session 7 · T1 Chapters 9–10 · sequence models, RNNs, BPTT, vanishing gradients, bidirectional and deep RNNs, GRU and LSTM

lesson.title: Why sequence models?
lesson.lead: In sequences **order matters** and context can come from far back.

items: Examples: language ("The cat sat on the ___"), stock prices and weather, speech, video, DNA.
Feed-forward networks fail here: fixed input size, no memory, and no parameter sharing across positions.

head: Dependency
Example
rows: "I grew up in France … I speak fluent ___" → French (needs words far back)

blocks.label: Key challenge
blocks.text: The model must learn what to **remember** and what to **forget**, for sequences of any length.

lesson.title: Autoregressive, Markov and latent models
lesson.lead: Three ways to model P(x₁, …, x_T). The **latent** (hidden-state) idea becomes the RNN.

blocks.text: P(x₁, …, x_T) = Πₜ P(xₜ | x₁, …, xₜ₋₁)
blocks.caption: autoregressive: each value depends on all previous ones; the history keeps growing

blocks.text: k-th order Markov:  P(xₜ | x₁…xₜ₋₁) ≈ P(xₜ | xₜ₋ₖ, …, xₜ₋₁)
blocks.caption: fixed window: tractable, but forgets long-range context (bigram k = 1, trigram k = 2)

blocks.text: Latent variable:  hₜ = f(xₜ, hₜ₋₁),   P(xₜ | x₁…xₜ₋₁) ≈ P(xₜ | hₜ)
blocks.caption: a fixed-size summary of the whole history, updated each step

blocks.text: Temperature example: Tₜ₊₁ = 0.8·Tₜ + 4. After 21 °C it predicts 0.8·21 + 4 = **20.8 °C**, then 0.8·20.8 + 4 = **20.64 °C**. Errors accumulate over multi-step forecasts, and the model only sees yesterday. A hidden state can encode the whole trend (warming then cooling).

lesson.title: The vanilla RNN
lesson.lead: Process one step at a time, carrying a **hidden state**, with the **same weights at every step**.

blocks.text: hₜ = φ(W_hh hₜ₋₁ + W_hx xₜ + b_h)          oₜ = W_ho hₜ + b_o          P(xₜ₊₁) = softmax(oₜ)
blocks.caption: φ is usually tanh; h₀ = 0 (or learned)

items: Parameter sharing: a fixed number of parameters for any sequence length, and patterns learned at one position transfer to others.
Unrolling: draw one copy per time step; every copy shares the same W_hx, W_hh, W_ho.

blocks.text: parameters = hd + h² + h + Vh + V = h(d + h + V + 1) + V
blocks.caption: d = 100, h = 256, V = 10,000 → 2,661,392

lesson.title: Training: BPTT
lesson.lead: **Backpropagation through time**: unroll the network, backprop as usual, and **sum** each shared weight's gradient over time.

blocks.text: L = Σₜ ℓₜ,   ℓₜ = −log P(xₜ | x₁…xₜ₋₁)   (cross-entropy per step)
blocks.caption: maximise likelihood = minimise negative log-likelihood; report the average per token

blocks.text: ∂L/∂hₜ = ∂ℓₜ/∂hₜ + (∂L/∂hₜ₊₁)(∂hₜ₊₁/∂hₜ),   ∂hₜ₊₁/∂hₜ = diag(1 − hₜ₊₁²) W_hh
∂L/∂W_hh = Σₜ δₜ hₜ₋₁ᵀ,   ∂L/∂W_hx = Σₜ δₜ xₜᵀ,   ∂L/∂W_ho = Σₜ (∂ℓₜ/∂oₜ) hₜᵀ
blocks.caption: δₜ = (∂L/∂hₜ) ⊙ (1 − hₜ²) for tanh

blocks.text: Output gradient with softmax + CE: ∂ℓₜ/∂oₜ = softmax(oₜ) − yₜ.

lesson.title: Vanishing and exploding gradients
lesson.lead: BPTT multiplies the same Jacobian again and again, so gradients shrink or blow up **exponentially** in sequence length.

blocks.text: ∂L/∂h₁ = ∂L/∂h_T · Πₜ diag(φ′(zₜ)) W_hh
Effect: early steps get almost no learning signal, so long-range patterns ("France … French", yearly seasonality) aren't learned.

blocks.label: Solutions
blocks.text: Fixes: **LSTM / GRU** gates, careful initialisation, skip connections; **gradient clipping** for exploding gradients.

lesson.title: Bidirectional and deep RNNs
lesson.lead: Bidirectional RNNs read **both directions**; deep RNNs **stack** recurrent layers.

blocks.text: h→ₜ = φ(W→ h→ₜ₋₁ + …),   h←ₜ = φ(W← h←ₜ₊₁ + …),   hₜ = [h→ₜ ; h←ₜ],   oₜ = W_ho hₜ + b_o

head: Use bidirectional
Don't
rows: Whole sequence available: text classification, named-entity recognition ("I met Paris in Paris"), translation encoders
Real-time / streaming, language modelling, forecasting (the future can't be used)

blocks.text: Bi-RNN parameters double the recurrent part, and the output layer sees 2h features. Example: d = 100, h = 128 each way, V = 10,000 → 29,312 + 29,312 + (10,000 × 256 + 10,000) = **2,628,624**.
Deep (stacked) RNNs
hₜ⁽ℓ⁾ = φ(W_hh⁽ℓ⁾ hₜ₋₁⁽ℓ⁾ + W_hx⁽ℓ⁾ hₜ⁽ℓ⁻¹⁾ + b⁽ℓ⁾),   hₜ⁽⁰⁾ = xₜ

Lower layers learn simple patterns (characters, phonemes, short trends); higher layers learn abstract ones. Gradients vanish through **both** time and depth, so use 2–4 layers with LSTM/GRU, residual connections and layer norm.

lesson.title: GRU: gated recurrent unit
lesson.lead: Two sigmoid **gates** decide what to reset and how much to update.

blocks.text: rₜ = σ(W_r xₜ + U_r hₜ₋₁ + b_r)          zₜ = σ(W_z xₜ + U_z hₜ₋₁ + b_z)
h̃ₜ = tanh(W_h xₜ + U_h (rₜ ⊙ hₜ₋₁) + b_h)          hₜ = zₜ ⊙ hₜ₋₁ + (1 − zₜ) ⊙ h̃ₜ

head: Gate
rows: Ignore the past when forming the candidate (new topic)

blocks.label: Convention
blocks.text: This deck's convention: hₜ = z ⊙ hₜ₋₁ + (1 − z) ⊙ h̃, so z = 1 means **keep the old state**. D2L uses the same convention; some sources swap it. Read the equation given in the question.
Why it helps: ∂hₜ/∂hₜ₋₁ contains the term zₜ, a direct additive path with no weight matrix or activation derivative, like a residual connection.
GRU parameters = 3(hd + h² + h) + Vh + V
blocks.caption: d = 100, h = 256 → 274,176 before the output layer

lesson.title: LSTM: long short-term memory
lesson.lead: LSTM keeps a separate **cell state cₜ** (long-term memory) controlled by three gates.

blocks.text: fₜ = σ(W_f xₜ + U_f hₜ₋₁ + b_f)    iₜ = σ(W_i xₜ + U_i hₜ₋₁ + b_i)    oₜ = σ(W_o xₜ + U_o hₜ₋₁ + b_o)
c̃ₜ = tanh(W_c xₜ + U_c hₜ₋₁ + b_c)    cₜ = fₜ ⊙ cₜ₋₁ + iₜ ⊙ c̃ₜ    hₜ = oₜ ⊙ tanh(cₜ)

head: Gate
Decides
rows: What to erase from the cell state
How much of the candidate c̃ to write
What part of the cell to expose as hₜ

blocks.text: **Why it solves vanishing gradients:** ∂cₜ/∂cₜ₋₁ = fₜ. With the forget gate open (f ≈ 1), the gradient flows along the cell "highway" with no weight multiplication.
LSTM parameters = 4(hd + h² + h) + Vh + V
blocks.caption: d = 100, h = 256 → 365,568 before the output layer

lesson.title: Time-series forecasting
lesson.lead: RNNs learn temporal patterns, trends and seasonality straight from the data.

blocks.text: Deck example: 7 days of [temp, humidity, pressure] → LSTM (h = 64) → ŷ = W_o h₇ + b_o, **multivariate in, univariate out**, MSE loss. Evaluate with MSE, RMSE (same units as y) and MAE (robust to outliers).
Applications: finance, weather, energy demand, patient vital signs, IoT sensor anomaly detection.

worked.title: RNN forward pass over three steps
worked.answer: h₃ = (0.734, 0.642). The same two matrices were used at every step. Check it in the Lab bench.

worked.title: Parameter counts: RNN vs GRU vs LSTM

problem.text: d = 100 input features, h = 256 hidden units, V = 10,000 outputs. Count the parameters of each.

worked.answer: RNN 2,661,392 · GRU core 274,176 · LSTM core 365,568. The output layer dominates when V is large.

worked.title: How fast gradients vanish

problem.text: λ_max(W_hh) = 0.8 and |tanh′| ≈ 0.5 at each step. What fraction of the gradient survives 5, 10 and 20 steps back?

worked.answer: About 1%, 0.01% and 10⁻⁸: long-range dependencies can't be learned by a vanilla RNN.

worked.title: One GRU step (scalar)

problem.text: Scalar GRU, x = 1, hₜ₋₁ = 0.5, biases 0. r = σ(0.5x + 0.5h), z = σ(1.0x − 1.0h), h̃ = tanh(0.8x + 0.6(r·h)), hₜ = z·hₜ₋₁ + (1 − z)·h̃.

worked.answer: hₜ = 0.599: about 62% old state and 38% new candidate.

worked.title: One LSTM step (scalar)
worked.answer: cₜ = 1.029, hₜ = 0.481. The cell can grow past 1; h is squashed by tanh and gated by o.

worked.title: Autoregressive temperature forecast

problem.text: Observed 20, 22, 25, 24, 21 °C. Model Tₜ₊₁ = 0.8Tₜ + 4. Predict days 6 and 7.

worked.answer: 20.8 °C, then 20.64 °C. First-order models only see yesterday and their errors accumulate. A hidden state captures the trend.

labs.title: RNN step-through and parameter counter
labs.intro: Enter W_hx, W_hh and a sequence. Every hidden state is computed with tanh, and the counter compares RNN, GRU, LSTM and bidirectional sizes.
tryThis: Scale W_hh up (e.g. 2 0; 0 2) and watch the states saturate near ±1.
Add an output matrix W_ho to see oₜ.
In the counter set V = 10,000 to reproduce the deck's 2,661,392.

formulas.name: RNN
formulas.formula: hₜ = tanh(W_hh hₜ₋₁ + W_hx xₜ + b_h);  oₜ = W_ho hₜ + b_o

formulas.name: GRU
formulas.formula: r = σ(·), z = σ(·), h̃ = tanh(W_h x + U_h(r ⊙ h₋₁)), h = z ⊙ h₋₁ + (1 − z) ⊙ h̃

formulas.name: LSTM
formulas.formula: f, i, o = σ(·); c̃ = tanh(·); c = f ⊙ c₋₁ + i ⊙ c̃; h = o ⊙ tanh(c)

formulas.name: Gated parameters
formulas.formula: GRU 3(hd + h² + h) · LSTM 4(hd + h² + h)

formulas.name: Bidirectional
formulas.formula: hₜ = [h→ₜ; h←ₜ]; recurrent parameters doubled; output sees 2h
